messages:
deploy-bot: Canary deploy finished for service=embedder image=embedder:v2026.03.14-4 (canary pool) — starting health checks. Initial rollout 10% traffic. Observed elevated errors during warmup window, escalating if persists.

pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PD alert fired: SERVICE_EMBEDDER_CANARY_FAILED (severity: critical) — paging on-call: sylvia chen

incident-bot: page fired for embedder-canary-failure — trigger=5xx_rate>3% over 60s, window=5m. See traces: https://observability.redwood/embedder/canary/3412345678

sylvia chen: acked. I'm on it — pinging dev.

marta rios: on way. quick note: any customer-facing 5xx yet?

sylvia chen: yes seeing 4% 5xx (mostly 502/503) and p95 latency jumped from ~400ms to ~2.2s for canary hosts. Dashboard: https://dash/embedder/canary?window=15m

devon liu: pulling logs and kernel traces. initial grep shows GPU OOMs on canary nodes during attention kernel runs.

devon liu: snippet from canary log:
```
[2026-03-14T22:14:03Z] ERROR embedder: OOM on GPU0 during attention_kernel (model=embedder, batch=8, seq=2048)
[2026-03-14T22:14:04Z] WARN  runtime: evicting KV cache entries
[2026-03-14T22:14:05Z] ERROR http: upstream 502 for request id=xx-yy-zz
```

omar shah: looks like the new quantization change in v2026.03.14-4 reduced memory headroom for long sequences. rolling canary traffic amplified seq=2048 paths.

marta rios: ok — we need fast mitigation. options: 1) rollback canary to prev stable 2) divert canary traffic to stable nodes 3) patch quick config (reduce seq or disable new kernel). thoughts?

sylvia chen: rollback seems safest given OOMs. can we do a quick rollback and then run smaller canary with seq cap?

devon liu: preparing rollback command. will execute once ops confirms.

ops-bot: detected rollback consent from on-call group. executing staged rollback.

devon liu: running rollback now:
```
rk-deploy rollback --service embedder --to-tag v2026.03.13-9 --staged --timeout 300s --reason "canary OOM regression"
```

ops-bot: rollback started: 10% -> 0% canary over 60s, housekeeping: drain-canary.sh, reassign-tasks, update-route.

pagerduty-bot: alert acknowledged by sylvia chen — escalation paused.

sylvia chen: switching monitoring to stable pool and watching error rate. please keep raw logs attached here.

omar shah: observing rollback progress — canary instances terminated and replaced with v2026.03.13-9. GPU memory errors stop on those hosts.

ops-bot: rollback completion: 100% rollback (canary removed) — total time 95s.

support-bot: creating high-priority support ticket ACME-789 for AcmeAnalytics (reported 3 failures) and auto-notifying CS.

devon liu: post-rollback metrics: p95 down to 380ms, 5xx rate dropped to 0.2% (5m window). Latency and error rate trending to baseline.

marta rios: good. can we confirm which customers saw errors and the window for error attribution?

sylvia chen: early estimate: ~3 external customers had requests hit the canary (AcmeAnalytics, BrightDataLabs, internal-ci). error window ~22:14:00–22:16:20 UTC. I've added a timeline in the incident doc.

marta rios: I'll take postmortem and customer comms. sylvia, please hand off follow-ups (logs, traces, rollout artifact).

sylvia chen: handing off to marta. Summary for PM/Oncall:
- root cause: memory regression introduced by quantization kernel change in v2026.03.14-4 causing OOMs under long sequences in canary pool
- impact: ~4% canary error rate, ~3 external customers observed errors for ~2m20s
- mitigation: rollback to v2026.03.13-9 within 95s, traffic restored to stable pool, errors resolved
- next steps: revert kernel change on branch, add e2e canary for long-seq paths, add seq-length guard in deployment config, update rollout runbook

sylvia chen: closing PD incident. moving to "postmortem_needed" and assigning to marta rios. on-call until 23:00UTC then hand to oncall-next.

marta rios: got it — I'll assemble the postmortem and coordinate customer notes. thanks all for quick responses :thumbsup:

devon liu: leaving a gist with logs and the failing kernel patch: https://gist.github.com/redwood/devon/embedder-oom-logs

sylvia chen: handing final ack and passing to marta for follow-up. //thread closed
